hints: Evaluate $\int 6x\ln x\,dx$ by parts with $u=\ln x$ and $dv=6x\,dx$.
Apply the limits $1$ and $a$, remembering that $\ln1=0$, and set the resulting expression equal to $4$.
Rearrange to isolate $\ln a$ and divide by the appropriate power of $a$.
Exponentiate both sides to reach the stated fixed-point equation exactly.
walkthrough:
Use integration by parts $\int u\dfrac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}\,\mathrm{d}x = uv - \int v\dfrac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}\,\mathrm{d}x$ on $\int 6x\ln x\,\mathrm{d}x$:
$$u = \ln x \implies \dfrac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{1}{x}$$
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x} = 6x \implies v = \int 6x\,\mathrm{d}x = 3x^2$$

Substitute into the parts formula:
$$\int 6x\ln x\,\mathrm{d}x = 3x^2\ln x - \int 3x^2\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x = 3x^2\ln x - \int 3x\,\mathrm{d}x = 3x^2\ln x - \dfrac{3}{2}x^2$$

Evaluate the definite integral between the limits $1$ and $a$:
$$\left[ 3x^2\ln x - \dfrac{3}{2}x^2 \right]_1^a = \left(3a^2\ln a - \dfrac{3}{2}a^2\right) - \left(3(1)^2\ln(1) - \dfrac{3}{2}(1)^2\right)$$
$$\text{Since } \ln(1) = 0: \quad = 3a^2\ln a - \dfrac{3}{2}a^2 - \left(0 - \dfrac{3}{2}\right) = 3a^2\ln a - \dfrac{3}{2}a^2 + \dfrac{3}{2}$$

Isolate $3a^2\ln a$ on the left-hand side:
$$3a^2\ln a = 4 - \dfrac{3}{2} + \dfrac{3}{2}a^2 = \dfrac{5}{2} + \dfrac{3}{2}a^2 = \dfrac{5 + 3a^2}{2}$$

hints: Use the equation from part (a), rather than numerically evaluating the original integral, to define a continuous root function.
For example, rearrange it to $f(x)=6x^2\ln x-3x^2-5$.
Evaluate $f(2)$ and $f(2.1)$ and display their opposite signs.
Invoke continuity on $[2,2.1]$ to verify that the required root lies between the endpoints.
walkthrough:
Define the continuous function $f(x) = 6x^2\ln x - 3x^2 - 5$ representing the equation $6a^2\ln a - 3a^2 - 5 = 0$:
$$f(x) = 3x^2(2\ln x - 1) - 5$$

Evaluate $f(x)$ at $x = 2$:
$$f(2) = 6(2^2)\ln 2 - 3(2^2) - 5 = 24(0.693147) - 12 - 5 = 16.6355 - 17 = -0.3645 < 0$$
$$\left(\text{or using the fixed-point form } g(x) = x - \exp\left[\dfrac{1}{6}\left(\dfrac{5}{x^2} + 3\right)\right]: \quad g(2) = 2 - 2.0306 = -0.0306 < 0\right)$$

Conclude using the intermediate value theorem:
$$\text{Since } f(x) \text{ is continuous on } [2, 2.1] \text{ and } f(2) < 0 \text{ while } f(2.1) > 0,$$
$$\text{there is a sign change. Hence the root } a \text{ lies between } 2 \text{ and } 2.1.$$

hints: Take $a_1=2$ and repeatedly substitute each output into the right-hand side, recording every iterate to 4 decimal places.
Continue until the values are stable enough to justify the final result to 2 decimal places.
walkthrough:
Set up the iteration formula $a_{n+1} = \exp\left[\dfrac{1}{6}\left(\dfrac{5}{a_n^2} + 3\right)\right]$ starting with initial guess $a_1 = 2$:
$$a_2 = \exp\left[\dfrac{1}{6}\left(\dfrac{5}{2^2} + 3\right)\right] = \exp\left[\dfrac{1}{6}(1.25 + 3)\right] = \exp\left(\dfrac{4.25}{6}\right) = \exp(0.708333) \approx 2.0306$$

Substitute $a_2 = 2.0306$ into the iteration formula to calculate subsequent iterates:
$$a_3 = \exp\left[\dfrac{1}{6}\left(\dfrac{5}{2.0306^2} + 3\right)\right] = \exp\left[\dfrac{1}{6}\left(\dfrac{5}{4.1233} + 3\right)\right] = \exp(0.70211) \approx 2.0180$$
$$a_4 = \exp\left[\dfrac{1}{6}\left(\dfrac{5}{2.0180^2} + 3\right)\right] = \exp\left[\dfrac{1}{6}\left(\dfrac{5}{4.0723} + 3\right)\right] = \exp(0.70464) \approx 2.0231$$
$$a_5 = \exp\left[\dfrac{1}{6}\left(\dfrac{5}{2.0231^2} + 3\right)\right] = \exp\left[\dfrac{1}{6}\left(\dfrac{5}{4.0929} + 3\right)\right] = \exp(0.70360) \approx 2.0210$$
$$a_6 = \exp\left[\dfrac{1}{6}\left(\dfrac{5}{2.0210^2} + 3\right)\right] \approx 2.0219$$

Round the converged value to 2 decimal places:
$$\text{Both } 2.0210 \text{ and } 2.0219 \text{ round to } 2.02:$$
$$a = 2.02$$
